newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi's Jeddah port to get new equipment - paper.
newsitem.headline: Saudi's Jeddah port to get new equipment - paper.

text.p: Jeddah port will take delivery of new equipment in 1997 which will help improve its productivity, the head of the ports authority was quoted on Tuesday as saying.
The daily al-Eqtisadiah newspaper quoted Mohammad Bakr as saying the port had awarded contracts worth 31 million riyals ($8.3 million) for 10 cranes, which would be delivered in the next nine months.
The ports authority would also buy two tugs to service large ships at the terminal. The tugs, worth 43 million riyals, would be delivered in early 1997, he said.
Bakr said the port's productivity had returned to normal, particularly in the past two weeks, and was currently handling 1,000 containers a day.

Shipping lines and agents have complained of long delays at Jeddah since the October change in management of the container terminal, saying the setbacks were prompting some to consider introducing container surcharges.
